title: Post-crisis adaptation is reorganizing AI expectations, practical consumption, identity, wellness, and cultural belonging
source_unit: Republic of Korea Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Korea’s Social and Cultural Trends in 2026: From Recovery to Adaptation
geography: South Korea; online discourse from Korean news, social media, online communities, and video platforms

observations.period: January-November 2025; online discourse analyzed for 2026 trend forecast

denominator.unit: online data items collected across news, social media, online communities, and video platforms

overarching_frame.value: K-Society is moving from post-crisis recovery toward adaptation and continued restructuring of everyday life

six_trends.value: Human-centered post-AI transition; being oneself and hyper-personalization; wellness transition; restrained practical consumption; K-culture and emotional economy; coexistence through emotional empathy

mechanism.value: Crisis adaptation is being expressed simultaneously through technology expectations, identity, spending, health, culture, and social relations

observations.method: Korean Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism text and keyword analysis of large-scale online data collected during 2025.
observations.uncertainty: Online discourse is not population prevalence; platform composition, keyword selection, algorithmic visibility, and media attention may shape the observed trend signals.
observations.subgroup: Online participants and communities represented in Korean news, social platforms, online communities, and video services; offline and less-connected groups may be underrepresented.
observations.counterinterpretation: The six trends may reflect a government-curated interpretive framework and media salience rather than durable changes in behavior, spending, or social norms.

observations.period: 2025 year-on-year online discourse; AI governance and social expectations

ai_mentions.unit: percent year-on-year increase in online mentions of AI

ai_policy_mentions.unit: percent year-on-year increase in AI-related policy keywords

ai_security_mentions.unit: percent year-on-year increase in AI-related security keywords

ai_regulation_mentions.unit: percent year-on-year increase in AI-related regulation keywords

mechanism.value: AI adoption is accompanied by a governance conversation about employment, safety, fairness, security, and institutional responsibility

observations.method: MCST keyword-trend comparison for AI-related terms in the 2025 online corpus.
observations.uncertainty: Keyword growth measures attention, not technology adoption, risk incidence, public consensus, or policy effectiveness; percentage changes may be sensitive to small baselines.
observations.subgroup: People and organizations participating in Korean online discourse about AI, including technology users, workers, policymakers, and consumers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Increased policy and security language can indicate informed governance attention or media amplification rather than rising perceived danger or opposition to AI.

observations.period: 2025 year-on-year online discourse; identity and practical consumption

being_oneself_mentions.unit: percent year-on-year increase in related online mentions

consumption_mentions.unit: percent year-on-year increase in consumption-related online mentions

value_for_money.value: Value for money was the largest keyword within consumption-related discourse

consumption_frame.value: Practical restraint is framed as rational expense management and alternative consumption, not simply reduced spending

mechanism.value: Household constraint can be culturally reframed as agency, efficiency, and individualized life design

observations.method: MCST keyword analysis of online discourse concerning identity, self-direction, consumption, and value.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not measure actual household budgets, purchases, income groups, or whether practical consumption is voluntary adaptation versus financial necessity.
observations.subgroup: Online consumers and identity-oriented communities, with unknown representation by income, age, geography, and offline consumption behavior.
observations.counterinterpretation: Value-for-money discourse may reflect ordinary consumer search behavior or marketing language rather than a broad cultural shift toward restraint.

observations.period: 2025 year-on-year online discourse; K-culture and emotional economy

k_culture_mentions.unit: percent year-on-year increase in K-culture-related online mentions

cultural_identity.value: K-culture is described as expanding beyond content consumption into emotional and economic value linked to fandom and cultural pride

empathy_and_coexistence.value: The forecast identifies emotional empathy as a basis for coexistence alongside performance and achievement

mechanism.value: Cultural participation can operate simultaneously as consumption, identity, national image, emotional affiliation, and economic activity

observations.method: MCST keyword analysis and interpretive synthesis of online cultural discourse, fandom activity, and related terms.
observations.uncertainty: Online mentions do not establish audience size, cultural export revenue, offline belonging, or the distribution of benefits across creators, firms, and communities.
observations.subgroup: K-culture audiences, fandom communities, creators, cultural firms, and participants in Korean online cultural discourse.
observations.counterinterpretation: Cultural pride and emotional language may be concentrated among highly engaged fans and may not represent broader national identity or social cohesion.

related_sources.claim: Official English-language Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism site.

boundary: This record adds a comparative cultural-consumer route from post-crisis adaptation through AI governance attention, individualized identity, practical consumption, wellness, K-culture, fandom, and emotional coexistence. It is a government trend forecast derived from online keyword analysis, not a representative public-opinion survey, behavioral panel, causal cultural evaluation, or proof of population-wide change.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official MCST English press-release page was reviewed for corpus size, keyword extraction, six-trend taxonomy, AI, identity, consumption, K-culture, and emotional-coexistence findings.
